intended_object: A comparison isomorphism. It identifies the k-points of the base change to k of the 𝔽₂ coordinate Hopf algebra (of the F4 short-root carrier group, a quotient of the coordinate ring of GL₂₆) with the library's matrix-valued carrier points `points k`. This is the canonical isomorphism G_k(k) ≅ G(k). Inferred from the docstring and the body.
explanation: The declaration is a group isomorphism built by composing two existing maps. The first is the general base-change adjunction on points, `AlgHom.baseChangePointsMulEquiv`, which says that k-algebra maps from k ⊗ Q to k correspond to 𝔽₂-algebra maps from Q to k. The second is `coordinatePointsEquiv`, which identifies points of the quotient Hopf algebra with the subgroup of GL₂₆ cut out by the defining ideal. It defines no new mathematical notion. It is a bridging device that lets the library move between its Hopf-algebra points and its concrete matrix carrier points. The underlying fact, that points of a base change are points of the original scheme, is a canonical identification. That makes it a technical construction rather than a definition to check against a textbook notion. As a construction it is sensible: both parts are the canonical maps, and the composition has the stated type.
